claims.text: The target material is a complex multiphase alloy containing metastable phases.
The target alloy has a heterogeneous microstructure before processing.
The proposed framework integrates advanced free-energy sampling with non-equilibrium statistical methods.
The framework can concurrently predict and control metastable phase evolution during dynamic thermo-mechanical processing.
The framework can concurrently promote microstructure refinement during dynamic thermo-mechanical processing.
The framework can optimize alloy properties during dynamic thermo-mechanical processing.
The proposed approach computationally maps the free-energy landscape under rapid thermal cycling and mechanical deformation.
The free-energy landscape governs transitions between competing metastable phases.
The free-energy landscape influences grain-size evolution.
Sampling free-energy barriers associated with metastable phase transitions identifies optimal processing windows.
The identified processing windows refine the microstructure while stabilizing desired phase compositions.
Simultaneous microstructure refinement and stabilization of desired phase compositions optimize material properties.
The proposed method will improve the balance among phase stability, microstructure refinement, and mechanical, thermal, or functional properties relative to traditional sequential processing.
Traditional thermo-mechanical treatments do not explicitly model or predict the free-energy landscape during non-equilibrium processing.
Accurate application of the approach requires a sufficiently well-defined free-energy landscape.
Complex or highly sensitive material systems may exhibit unforeseen dynamics that limit the approach.
